How to Buy Tax Deeds and Tax Liens in Jackson County, Florida

If you’re looking to invest in Florida real estate or earn a return through tax liens, Jackson County offers a solid opportunity. Their tax sales are held online and are open to everyone, whether you’re local or out-of-state.

Let’s break down how it works in plain English.

Understanding Tax Certificate Sales in Jackson County

What Happens First
Property taxes become delinquent on April 1. The county advertises unpaid taxes in the local newspaper for three weeks in a row. Once advertised, the tax lien (called a tax certificate) is put up for online auction.

How Do Bids Work
Bidding starts at 18% interest. Investors bid by offering the lowest interest rate they’re willing to accept. The lowest bidder wins the tax certificate.

What Happens After the Sale
The property owner has up to two years to pay off the taxes and interest. If they don’t pay within that time, the investor can apply for a tax deed, which may lead to owning the property.

How Tax Deed Sales Work in Jackson County

Applying for a Deed
After the 2-year waiting period, the certificate holder can apply for a tax deed sale. The Clerk of Court schedules the property for public online auction.

How the Auction Works
The opening bid covers unpaid taxes, fees, and interest. The property is sold as-is to the highest bidder. All bidders must register and pay a deposit—$200 or 5% of your max bid, whichever is greater.

What Happens to Extra Money
If the property sells for more than the amount owed, that extra money (called surplus funds) might go to the former property owner or other claimants. The Clerk of Court handles these cases.

Why Jackson County is Worth a Look

Real Estate Snapshot

  • One of Florida’s more affordable rural counties
  • Great for land flippers, small investors, and first-time buyers
  • Lots of vacant land and older homes go up for auction
  • Many lots come with multiple acres—perfect for privacy or farming

Location Perks

  • Right along I-10, which connects to major cities like Pensacola and Tallahassee
  • Growing interest in the area for distribution hubs and rural living

Pro Tips for First-Time Investors

  • Always do your homework on the property. Check the location, taxes, and if there are any liens or title issues.
  • Remember: all sales are final. Properties are sold as-is.
  • Don’t skip the due diligence—you could end up with a property that has major issues.

FAQs About Jackson County Tax Sales

Can anyone join these auctions?
Yes. Anyone, even out-of-state or international investors, can register and bid.

Is there a cost to register?
Registration is free, but you’ll need to place a deposit to start bidding.

What happens if no one bids on a tax lien?
The certificate is sold to the county. Later, it may be available for over-the-counter purchase.

Are tax deed sales risky?
They can be if you don’t research the property first. Always check for other liens and conditions.

Where can I get updates?

Just remember: the key to success is doing your research. Understand the process, know what you’re buying, and track the auction calendar.
